'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[Somali Civil War (2009–present)|Somali Civil War]]
**[[American military intervention in Somalia (2007–present)|American military intervention in Somalia]]
***The [[United States]] conducts a drone strike against [[Al-Shabaab (militant group)|Al-Shabaab]] militants near the [[Somalia]] town of [[Galkayo]], making it the first military action in the country that was carried by the [[Presidency of Joe Biden|Biden administration]]. [https://www.voanews.com/africa/us-strikes-al-shabab-somalia-first-time-six-months (VOA)]
*[[Mali War]]
**A knifeman wounds [[Mali]]an [[List of heads of state of Mali|President]] [[Assimi Goïta]] in the arm at a [[mosque]] in [[Bamako]]. The perpetrator is arrested, and the attack is described as an [[assassination]] attempt. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2021/7/20/knife-attack-mali-interim-president-assimi-goita (Al Jazeera)]
*[[Israel–Lebanon relations]]
**The [[Israeli military]] bombs southern [[Lebanon]] after rockets are fired into [[Israel]]i territory from these locations. [[Prime Minister of Israel|Israeli Prime Minister]] [[Naftali Bennett]] justifies the air strike by stating that "anyone who tries to harm us will pay a painful price in return". [https://apnews.com/article/middle-east-israel-lebanon-78a4beebadf1ca349d2c37702183df58 (AP)]

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*[[2021 Henan floods]]
**Major floods in [[Henan]], [[China]], caused by 20cm of rain per hour, affect subways and kill at least 12 people in the [[underground rail]] system of [[Zhengzhou]]. [https://www.nytimes.com/2021/07/20/world/asia/china-flooding-zhengzhou-subway.html (''The New York Times'')]

'''Health and environment'''
*[[COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Asia]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Iran]]
****[[Iran]] reports a record 27,444 new cases of [[COVID-19]] in the past 24 hours, thereby bringing the national total of cases to 3,576,148. [https://apnews.com/article/lifestyle-middle-east-health-iran-coronavirus-pandemic-b6dd033e37b62b46f9b61266230f4475 (AP)]
****Iran imposes a week-long [[COVID-19 lockdowns|lockdown]] in [[Tehran]] and the surrounding [[Regions of Iran|region]] in the province of [[Alborz Province|Alborz]] where all [[bazaar]]s, public offices, market places, restaurants, gyms, and movie theatres are closed, due to an increase in the number of COVID-19 cases. [https://apnews.com/article/lifestyle-middle-east-health-iran-coronavirus-pandemic-9f2654073620e5119ff85d1ab10331d9 (AP)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Laos]]
****[[Laos]] reports a record 170 new cases of COVID-19 in the past 24 hours, thereby bringing the nationwide total of confirmed cases to 3,710. [https://laotiantimes.com/2021/07/20/laos-confirms-record-number-of-covid-19-cases-as-migrant-workers-return/?amp (''The Laotian Times'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Myanmar]]
****[[Nyan Win (NLD)|Nyan Win]], a senior advisor to ousted leader [[Aung San Suu Kyi]], dies in hospital after contracting COVID-19 in prison, amid an increase in the number of COVID-19 cases in the country. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2021/7/20/jailed-myanmar-politician-nyan-win-dies-from-covid (Al Jazeera)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in South Korea]]
****[[South Korea]]n [[Prime Minister of South Korea|Prime Minister]] [[Kim Boo-kyum]] and [[Ministry of National Defense (South Korea)|Minister for National Defnese]] [[Suh Wook]] apologize for the outbreak of COVID-19 aboard the destroyer ''Munmu the Great'' off the coast of [[Africa]]. Currently, nearly 250 of the 301 unvaccinated crew aboard the ship have contracted COVID-19. Prime Minister Kim says "I apologize for having failed to take better care of the health of our soldiers who devoted themselves to the country". [https://www.reuters.com/world/asia-pacific/skorea-leaders-apologise-navy-ship-covid-19-outbreak-amid-vaccine-furore-2021-07-20/ (Reuters)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in North America]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Canada]]
****[[COVID-19 pandemic in Alberta]]
*****[[Alberta]] reports 98 hospitalizations, making it the first time since October 2020 that less than 100 people have been hospitalized. [https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/edmonton/covid-19-hospitalizations-drop-below-100-as-alberta-reports-69-new-cases-1.6110263 (CBC)]
****[[COVID-19 pandemic in Ontario]]
*****[[Ontario]] reports that over 8 million people in the province has been fully vaccinated. [https://toronto.ctvnews.ca/ontario-reports-under-130-new-cases-of-covid-19-over-8-million-fully-vaccinated-1.5515979 (CTV)] 
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in the United States]]
****[[COVID-19 pandemic in California]]
*****[[Pasadena, California|Pasadena]] becomes the first city in [[Southern California]] to require [[Vaccination|vaccinations]] for employees. However, the mandate will not be in effect until it receives a full approval by the [[Food and Drug Administration]]. [https://losangeles.cbslocal.com/2021/07/20/pasadena-face-mask-covid-vaccine-mandate/ (KCBS-TV)]
****[[COVID-19 pandemic in New Hampshire]]
*****[[New Hampshire]] surpasses 100,000 cases of COVID-19. [https://www.wmur.com/article/new-hampshire-100000-covid-19-cases/37083016# (WMUR-TV)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Australia]]
***Lockdown restrictions return in [[South Australia]] after an increase in the number of COVID-19 cases. Three Australian states, and roughly half the national population, are now under strict lockdowns. [https://www.theguardian.com/australia-news/2021/jul/20/south-australia-covid-19-lockdown-restrictions-sa-adelaide-update-coronavirus-face-mask-rules-explained-masks-indoors-singing-dancing-weddings-public-transport-new-south-wales (''The Guardian'')]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Russia]]
***[[Russia]] surpasses six million cases of COVID-19, becoming the fourth country to do so after the [[United States]], [[India]], and [[Brazil]]. [https://m.akipress.com/news:660758:Russia_passes_6_million_coronavirus_cases/ (AKIPress)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Zimbabwe]]
***[[COVID-19 vaccination in Zimbabwe]]
****[[Zimbabwe]]an [[Government of Zimbabwe|authorities]] order compulsory vaccinations for [[civil servant]]s and also reduce the number of government workers to physically report for duty to 25% in an attempt to reduce the local transmission of COVID-19. [https://www.rte.ie/news/world/2021/0720/1236295-zimbabwe-mandatory-vaccination/ (RTÉ)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Peru]]
***The [[Peruvian]] [[Ministry of Health (Peru)|Ministry of Health]] announces that the country will purchase 20 million doses of the [[Sputnik V COVID-19 vaccine|Sputnik V vaccine]]. [https://www.reuters.com/article/health-coronavirus-peru/peru-strikes-deal-to-purchase-20-mln-doses-of-sputnik-v-vaccine-idUSL1N2OW17P (Reuters)]

'''International relations'''
*[[Lithuania–Taiwan relations]]
**[[Taiwan]] announces that it will be opening a representative office in [[Vilnius]], [[Lithuania]]. This comes amid warming relations between the two nations and the opening of a Lithuanian office in [[Taipei]]. The office will be known as the Taiwanese Representative Office in Lithuania, making it the first [[List of diplomatic missions of Taiwan|Taiwanese diplomatic mission]] in Europe to include Taiwan in its name. [https://www.taiwannews.com.tw/en/news/4252741 (Taiwan News)]

'''Law and crime'''
*A second criminal investigation is opened into the husband of [[Popular Force]] leader and former presidential candidate [[Keiko Fujimori]] over allegations of [[money laundering]]. [https://www.radiohc.cu/en/noticias/internacionales/264619-peruvian-public-prosecutors-office-opens-case-against-keiko-fujimoris-husband (Radio Havana Cuba)]

'''Politics and elections'''
*[[COVID-19 pandemic in Tunisia]], [[Impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on politics]]
**[[Tunisia]]n [[Prime Minister of Tunisia|Prime Minister]] [[Hichem Mechichi]] fires [[Ministry of Public Health (Tunisia)|Minister for Public Health]] [[Faouzi Mehdi]]  and appoints [[Mohamed Trabelsi]] as caretaker Minister for Public Health amid a collapse of the nation's healthcare system due to an increase in COVID-19 cases. [https://www.aa.com.tr/en/africa/tunisian-health-minister-sacked-as-covid-19-cases-surge/2310386 (Anadolu Agency)]
*During a visit to [[Washington, D.C.]], Belarusian opposition leader [[Sviatlana Tsikhanouskaya]] asks the [[Presidency of Joe Biden|Biden administration]] to impose sanctions on companies in [[Belarus]] in order to put pressure on the government of [[President of Belarus|President]] [[Alexander Lukashenko]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/europe/belarus-opposition-leader-asks-more-us-sanctions-2021-07-20/ (Reuters)]

'''Science and technology'''
*[[Blue Origin]], [[Blue Origin NS-16]]
**Blue Origin launches its first crew onboard its [[New Shepard]] rocket to outer space. The mission was crewed by American [[billionaire]] and Blue Origin founder [[Jeff Bezos]], his brother [[Mark Bezos]], pilot and [[Mercury 13]] candidate [[Wally Funk]] and Dutch student [[Oliver Daemen]]. Funk and Daemen respectively become the oldest and youngest people ever to travel to space. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/science-environment-57849364 (BBC News)]

'''Sports'''
*[[2021 NBA Finals]]
**In [[basketball]], the [[Milwaukee Bucks]] defeat the [[Phoenix Suns]] 105-98 in game 6 of the [[2021 NBA Finals|NBA Finals]], making it their first NBA championship since [[1971 NBA Finals|1971]]. [[Giannis Antetokounmpo]] is named [[NBA Finals Most Valuable Player Award|NBA Finals MVP]]. [https://www.jsonline.com/story/sports/nba/2021/07/20/giannis-antetokounmpo-bucks-win-first-nba-championship-50-years/8035210002/ (''Milwaukee Journal Sentinel'')]
